body:
Update from the 2026-08-28 run, with the evidence that has changed since this issue was filed.

I re-proposed `https://cursor.com/resources/grok-4-6-model-card.pdf` this morning without knowing #28 and #31 already existed — nothing in the agent's inputs (`state_summary.json`, `candidates.json`, `open_issues.json`) records prior rejections, and `open_issues.json` was empty this run because Phase B could not reach the GitHub API. The proposal was routed to needs-review again, so a third issue on the same URL is in the outbox. Apologies for the duplicate; please treat #28, #31 and the incoming one as one thread. (The underlying gap is logged to `friction.jsonl` this run.)

The new fact, verified today by downloading both files:

| | xAI (`media.x.ai/…/card-4p6-4cd2dc57.pdf`) | Cursor (`cursor.com/resources/grok-4-6-model-card.pdf`) |
|---|---|---|
| md5 | `7640cdde745a18a2390cd5fbde55fd55` | `5faf54cc75e26c987541719b7e2d56f1` |
| size | 540,844 B | 524,224 B |
| cover | Revision: 2026-08-17 | Revision: 2026-08-12 |

Word-level diff similarity is 0.705, so the two copies are no longer the same document by any measure except the stored launch-day fingerprint the dedup check matches against. xAI's changelog for the 08-17 revision reads: renumbered sections; added PartBench results and graph; added new DeepSearchQA results; KernelBenchInternal updated to v1.1; clarity updates; and "Corrected eval results on HackerBench v0.2, Self-harm, MASK, LAB". Cursor's copy is currently the only public edition carrying the pre-correction numbers for those four safety and behavioural evals.

When #28 was filed on 2026-08-13 the two files were byte-identical, so the "likely a mirror or moved copy" reading was reasonable then. It is no longer the situation. I have also corrected the `notes` on `xai-grok-4-6-model-card`, which still asserted byte-identity, to describe the divergence.

No action requested beyond adjudicating the three issues together. The structural ask — making the content-duplicate check publisher-aware so a launch-partner co-publication is distinguishable from a mirror — is already written up in `logs/PROPOSALS.md` under 2026-08-22.

body:
**Independent re-verification against the live source, 2026-08-30** (daily curation agent; no action taken on the corpus).

Every factual claim in this issue reproduces today. Evidence:

1. **The transparency page links only the new hash.** `https://www.anthropic.com/transparency/model-report` (HTTP 200, browser UA) contains exactly one `Claude%20Opus%205%20System%20Card.pdf` link, and it is `b514064af1408018e64b1ad24e7d5e75850b4ffd`. The hash the corpus holds, `c5fbac3f0b1280a933ebd26d3cb8bb9f5bdeaf48`, appears nowhere on the page.
2. **Both hashes still return 200**, so this move is invisible to link checking, as the issue states:
   - `c5fbac3f…` → 200, 15,981,937 bytes (held, orphaned)
   - `b514064a…` → 200, 15,994,568 bytes (currently linked)
3. **The Table 8.1.A edit is real and is a numbers change, not repagination.** Extracted both with `pdftotext`; the FrontierBench v0.1 row reads:
   - held `c5fbac3f`: `43.3 | 18.7 | 33.7 | 37.5`
   - live `b514064a`: `43.3 | 21.1 | 33.8 | 34.4`
   i.e. Opus 4.8 18.7→21.1, Fable 5 33.7→33.8, and GPT-5.6 Sol 37.5→34.4 — a downward revision to a competitor model's score in the headline capability table.
4. **The Harbor attribution is new.** The string "Harbor" occurs **0 times** in the held edition and **2 times** in the live one, including the added line *"FrontierBench results in this table are from Harbor's evaluations."*
5. **The refactoring note is new**: "refactor" occurs once in the held edition and twice in the live one.

Line counts after extraction: 7,212 (held) vs 7,239 (live).

**Assessment:** this is one document in two substantive editions, and the corpus currently holds the superseded one while Anthropic publishes the other. The 2026-08-18 "repagination only" finding was wrong. I did not re-propose, because an unchanged re-proposal would only file a second review issue on the same URL — the failure mode already visible in #28/#31/#32. This needs a human merge decision.

Related pattern found today and worth deciding alongside this: Anthropic's 2026-08-28 alignment paper links the Claude Opus 4.8 system card at `www-cdn.anthropic.com/0b4915911bb0d19eca5b5ee635c80fef830a37ea.pdf`, whose changelog stops at 2026-06-03, while the canonical `anthropic.com/claude-opus-4-8-system-card` serves an edition with corrections through 2026-06-17 (that one is byte-identical to what the corpus holds, sha256 `0df5d061…`, so no action needed there). Superseded-but-live CDN editions are evidently a recurring class, not a one-off.

body:
**Independent verification against the live sources, 2026-08-30** (daily curation agent; no action taken on the corpus).

**The duplicate flag is a false positive. These are two different documents.** I fetched both PDFs today and compared them mechanically:

| | held `meta-muse-spark-1-2-other` | proposed |
|---|---|---|
| URL | `research.meta.ai/static/muse-spark-1-2-methodology` | `research.meta.ai/static/muse-spark-1-2-multimodal-evaluation-methodology` |
| HTTP / size | 200, 81,397 B, 3 pages | 200, 83,986 B, 4 pages |
| Title | "Muse Spark 1.2 & Muse Code — Evaluation Methodology" | "Muse Spark 1.2 Multimodal Evaluation Methodology" |
| Benchmarks | Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSWE v1.1, GDPVal-AA v2 | BabyVision, PerceptionBench, ZeroBench, WorldVQA, SimpleVQA, ERQA, OmniSpatial, CharXiv, ChartMuseum, ChartQAPro, Wild Artifact Bench, Design Arena |

- **Benchmark overlap: zero.** Not one benchmark appears in both documents.
- **Word-level similarity: 0.128** (`difflib.SequenceMatcher` over 848 vs 1,173 words).
- The held document covers coding/agentic evaluation; the proposed one covers multimodal perception and reasoning. They are companion methodology reports for the same model, not two copies of one report.

The heuristic that fired — same publisher + doc_type + overlapping model names at a different URL — is doing its job, but the signal it keys on (both documents are about Muse Spark 1.2) is exactly what you would expect from a publisher that splits its evaluation methodology across modality-specific reports. Meta has now done this at least twice.

**Recommendation: admit the proposed document.** It passes the system-card test on its own terms — it is per-benchmark evaluation protocol for a named model, which is the content that sits in the evaluations section of a model card.

I deliberately did **not** re-propose it. The dedup check is deterministic and keys on publisher/doc_type/model_names, so an identical re-proposal would fire the same rule and file a second review issue for the same URL regardless of the evidence above — the exact multiplication visible in #28/#31/#32. This one needs a human to merge it (or to tell the pipeline that Meta's split methodology reports are a known-good shape).
